purpose: Professional settlement rules for supplier payments, supplier advances and direct third-party payments without creating fictitious Transtrade bank movements.

accounts.name: Due to Third Party / Settlement Payable

rules.normalSupplierPayment: Debit the actual supplier/broker liability component being settled and credit the selected Transtrade bank/cash account.
rules.supplierAdvanceFromOwnFunds: Debit Supplier / Broker Advances and credit selected Transtrade bank/cash. When a later supplier bill is approved, apply the advance against that supplier/Soda/truck with full allocation traceability.
rules.customerPaysSupplierAgainstExistingRecei: Debit the supplier liability or Supplier / Broker Advances, as applicable, and credit the identified customer receivable. No Transtrade bank movement is posted.
rules.customerPaysSupplierBeforeCustomerSaleRe: Debit Supplier / Broker Advances (or the existing supplier liability if already posted) and credit Customer Advances / Unapplied Receipts. Later allocate the customer advance when the sale is recognized.
rules.unrelatedThirdPartyPaysSupplier: Debit the supplier liability or Supplier / Broker Advances and credit Due to Third Party / Settlement Payable. No Transtrade bank movement is posted.
rules.groupEntityPaysAnotherEntitySupplier: Use explicit intercompany due-to/due-from treatment in both legal books; do not use ordinary Third Party Settlement.
rules.familyOrStaffPaysOnBehalf: Use the approved person-specific reimbursement payable when the payer is a configured family/staff person and the payment is genuinely on behalf of the business.
rules.allocation: If a payment/advance is explicitly linked to a Soda or truck/Pohanch, use that linkage. If it is only a general broker/supplier advance, do not guess the Soda; show it as unallocated and let Accounts confirm allocation.
rules.bankRule: A direct third-party settlement must never create a fictitious Transtrade bank or cash entry.
